rationale: A synthetic phenolic antioxidant used very widely in food and personal-care formulations worldwide and reviewed as such in the international literature. Permitted without limit in India (absent from IS 4707 Parts 1-4). Scored on the same global-proxy basis as triphenyl phosphate and benzyl butyl phthalate, both 0.45, but one step lower because BHT is typically used at very low concentrations and is often not separately declared.
source: Synthetic phenolic antioxidant review literature [global]; no India cosmetic survey located

rationale: Parent benzophenone (distinct from benzophenone-3/oxybenzone) is more often an impurity or packaging/fragrance contaminant than a deliberately added cosmetic ingredient; no India cosmetic-use survey found.
source: No India-specific source located; EU CMR (Omnibus VI) rationale only

rationale: Multiple India-based suppliers (BRM Chemicals; Sihauli Chemicals; Activeman) actively market benzophenone-3 for the Indian sunscreen and cosmetics industry; commercial availability confirmed, no quantitative product survey located.
source: India-based benzophenone-3 supplier listings (BRM Chemicals; Sihauli Chemicals; Activeman)

rationale: Bisphenol S was included in the analyte panel of the 114-sample Indian personal-care-product survey that measured bisphenol A - the authors purchased and quantified BPS standards alongside BPA, BPF, BPAF and four other bisphenols. This establishes that BPS is looked for as a cosmetic-relevant analyte in the Indian market. The per-compound detection frequency could not be obtained (full text not accessible), so no direct-measurement claim is made and the score is held at the category-proxy level rather than the 0.65-0.70 band BPA occupies. Note also that BPS reaches consumers substantially via thermal paper and packaging rather than as an added cosmetic ingredient, so its exposure pathway differs from the UV filters and preservatives in this set.
source: Jala et al., Chemosphere 297:134028 (2022), DOI 10.1016/j.chemosphere.2022.134028 - BPS in analyte panel; per-compound detection frequency not obtained

rationale: Permitted as a UV filter at 10% in all product types (IS 4707 Part 4:2022 Table 1 entry ii), so commercial sunscreen use is legal and plausible. Scored level with 4-MBC, which rests on the same regulatory-legality basis. Our own survey of 34 Indian sunscreen listings returned no declared homosalate, but most listings did not publish a full INCI, so this is an absence of data rather than evidence of absence.
source: Regulatory status, IS 4707 Part 4:2022; no India market study located

rationale: Permitted without any concentration limit in India (absent from IS 4707 Parts 1-4), and skin-lightening products are a large and well-documented segment of the Indian personal-care market. Scored above the 4-MBC baseline because the product category is established in India, but no compound-level Indian product survey or biomonitoring study was located.
source: India retail availability, author-verified; SPECIFIC LISTINGS STILL TO BE NAMED

rationale: Fragrance ingredient. India requires disclosure above 0.001% but sets no maximum concentration (IS 4707 Part 2:2025 Annex B entry 80), so it may legally appear at any level across fragranced products. Breadth of potential exposure is therefore high, but no Indian fragrance-ingredient survey was located and no compound-level data exists, so scored on the same category-level basis as the isomer-specific parabens (0.35).
source: No India fragrance-ingredient survey located; regulatory status IS 4707 Part 2:2025 Annex B entry 80

rationale: Permitted without limit in India (absent from IS 4707 Parts 1-4) and a standard ingredient in topical analgesic balms and oral-care products, both established Indian product categories. Scored level with kojic acid on the same category-level basis. No quantitative Indian product survey located.
source: No India market study located; category-level inference from the Indian OTC topical-analgesic market
